findings.note: TestResultSchemaVersionDistinct's second half cannot prove what its comment claims. The comment (manifest_test.go:109-111) says 'only a result carrying ResultSchemaVersion proves which constant the check uses', but SchemaVersion and ResultSchemaVersion are both 1 (manifest.go:23 and manifest.go:27), so a result at either constant is byte-identical and the loop asserting no 'unsupported schema version' blocker would pass whichever constant resultBlockers reads. The assertion is tautological until the two constants diverge; only the first half (ResultSchemaVersion+1 blocks) is load-bearing today.

The severity boundary is pinned from one side only. TestWaivedMediumFindingBlocks (manifest_test.go:247) asserts medium blocks under waived/accepted-risk/deferred/open, and TestFixedAndFalsePositiveClose uses critical, but nothing asserts that a low-severity finding with a non-closing disposition does NOT block. severityBlocks (manifest.go:641-643) could be widened to include SeverityLow without any test in this file failing, which would silently turn advisory shard findings into gate blockers.

Dead scaffolding in the new shell test: write_results declares ONLY and SKIP_CROSS parameters (tests/go/test-sharded-review.sh:57-59) whose branches at lines 64 and 76 select a subset of shards or suppress the cross-shard result, but all three call sites (lines 147, 179, 246) pass only two arguments. The partial-results and missing-cross-shard-result-after-a-fix paths those knobs exist to exercise are therefore never driven by this suite.

Weak new manifest assertions: tests/manifest/test-manifests.sh:41-42 check only that the stringified plugin manifest contains the substring 'workflow'. That matches any incidental occurrence (a description, a path segment, the word 'workflows' in unrelated prose) and would not fail if the fsm/workflow command entry itself were removed, unlike the sibling assertions above it which name concrete command ids such as 'epic-ready' and 'pr-ready'.
